pairs.subject: judge-calibration-and-drift
pairs.evidence: uat/rubric.md:30 The overlay defines judge agreement as an uncorrected raw pass ratio against the in-app tutor model without a human-labeled golden set or Cohen's kappa calibration, allowing uncalibrated judge outputs to drive release-gating verdicts.

techniques.evidence: uat/rubric.md:30 Calculates judge agreement as a raw ratio of agreement against the in-app tutor model rather than chance-corrected Cohen's kappa on a frozen human-labeled golden set.
uat/driver/verdict.cjs:142 Gating pass/fail verdicts are decided directly from uncalibrated judge checks without a pre-committed kappa trust bar or machine-readable trusted/untrusted boundary.
uat/README.md:58 Recertification reruns application journeys to check open product findings rather than running a scheduled recalibration sentinel over a pinned golden set.
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:370 Writes run findings to local run files rather than persisting calibration history under a reserved rubric namespace in a shared quality-score store.
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:85 Computes a memoryless point-to-point delta between two runs rather than maintaining a rolling window over historical cycles to catch slow slides.
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:41 Judge model was chosen by subscription constraint rather than evaluating discrimination spread between known-good and known-bad outputs on a golden set.
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:262 Metric regression alerting triggers on a hardcoded 10-point drop without measuring the judge's repeatability floor across repeated draws.
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:160 Treats switching judge models as an unbridgeable instrument confound rather than replaying the replacement over reference anchors with floor-based tolerance.
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:110 The judge system prompt is authored statically and is not fitted or tuned against human annotations.
uat/rubric.md:9 Scoring evaluates candidate outputs absolutely against rubric criteria and definitions of done rather than against an exemplar reference.
